chapters.title: Lecture 1 · Concept and characteristics of contemporary financial transactions
Lecture 2 · Ijtihad method and types of rights
Lecture 3 · Incorporeal rights: copyright, patents, trade names
Lecture 5 · Securities and the stock market
Lecture 9 · Sale, installment sale and Murabaha
Lecture 12 · Multi-level Marketing and pyramid scheme

questions.q: Which of the four categories of transactions does an endowment (waqf) belong to?
questions.e: Waqf is a gift with no return, so it sits with grants and wills under Donations.

questions.q: Forgiving a debt owed to you falls under which category?
questions.e: Dropping ends a right. Documentation, by contrast, protects one.

questions.q: A mortgage is an example of:
questions.e: Documentation covers mortgage, bail (warranty), and draft — instruments that secure an obligation.

questions.q: Property ownership no longer requires physically handing over the key because Property Registry Offices exist. Which of the four cases is this?
o: Rules updated due to progress or changed circumstances
Transactions formulated from several old forms
questions.e: The procedure changed; the underlying transaction did not. That is case 2.

questions.q: Calling usury "bank interest" is an example of:
o: A new case unknown in earlier ages
A new name for a transaction already ruled on
questions.e: Only the label changed; the ruling is unaffected. Hence the hadith about drinking khamr under another name.

questions.q: Murabaha is cited as an example of which case?
o: Transactions formulated from several old forms combined
questions.e: Murabaha merges more than one classical contract type into a single modern contract.

questions.q: Banknotes and corporate companies are given as examples of:
questions.e: Neither existed for earlier jurisprudents to rule on.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts acts of worship with transactions?
o: Worship is permitted by default; transactions are restricted by default
Worship is restricted by default; transactions are permitted by default
questions.e: Nothing is added to worship without a permitting text; nothing is forbidden in transactions without a clear prohibiting text.

questions.q: The hadith "If anyone introduces in our matter something which does not belong to it, it will be rejected" supports which principle?
o: The restriction principle for acts of worship
questions.e: It is the restriction principle, aimed at bid'ah in worship — not at transactions.

questions.q: Selling fish still in the sea is a textbook example of:
questions.e: Gharar: there is no guarantee the seller can deliver the goods paid for.

questions.q: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:275 is cited for which point?
o: Trade is permitted and riba forbidden
Wealth must not be consumed unjustly
The sea and earth are subjected to people
questions.e: 2:275 is the trade-permitted / riba-forbidden verse. 4:29 is the mutual-consent verse.

questions.q: Which set names the near-synonyms for newly emerged issues needing a ruling?
questions.e: E.O.I.F. — all four point at the same idea.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the nine qualifications of a researcher?
o: Deep mastery of the Arabic language
Awareness of the higher objectives of religion
questions.e: A judicial appointment is never listed. The nine are Q.H.I.A. plus S.H.M.R.U. (The slides group them into six; the exam follows the notes' nine.)

questions.q: In the eight steps to a ruling, what immediately follows searching the Qur'an and Sunnah?
o: Examining the Companions' sayings and arguments
questions.e: Order: pray, understand, texts, Companions, four imams, new sources, own opinion, refrain. (The slides show seven steps with no own-opinion step; the exam follows the notes' eight.)

questions.q: A scholar has exhausted every source and still cannot reach a legitimate rule. What should he do?
o: Follow the closest school of thought
Issue the most cautious fatwa available
Refrain from ruling — issue no fatwa
questions.e: Step 8 is explicit: refrain rather than guess.

questions.q: Which pair are the two shapes a right can take, per the lecture's definition?
questions.e: "An exclusive entitlement by which the Law establishes an authority or an obligation."

questions.q: The right of election and nomination is classified as:
questions.e: Political rights organise governance and its authorities.

questions.q: The inviolability of one's residence is an example of:
questions.e: General rights — inherent personality rights — need no second party.

questions.q: You are owed money by a debtor. Which financial right is that?
questions.e: The right points at a person's obligation, so it is Personal — also called a commitment.

questions.q: Which test sorts a private right into Family versus Financial?
o: Whether a second party is involved
Whether it could be evaluated with money
Whether it is established by the state
Whether it is permanent or temporary
questions.e: Family rights cannot be priced; financial rights can.

questions.q: How does fiqh define property (māl)?
o: Any tangible object that can be physically possessed
Anything with recognised value among people that may be lawfully utilised
Anything that can be bought and sold in a market
Any asset registered under an owner's name
questions.e: Value plus permissible utility — nothing in the formula requires the thing to be physical.

questions.q: Which of the three incorporeal rights is actually the oldest by the years given?
questions.e: The lecture lists them 1886, 1791, 1909 — so the list order is not the timeline.

questions.q: A book that only collects and abstracts existing information with no creative contribution is:
o: Protected exactly like any other work
Protected only for the financial right
Not considered innovation, so not protected the same way
Protected only if the author's name appears on it
questions.e: Interpreting, adding detail, correcting mistakes, or summarising for students would count as creating; mere collection does not.

questions.q: A work is published under a pseudonym. Who acts as the author's representative?
o: No one — the work is unprotected
questions.e: Name on the work means presumed author; no name means the publisher stands in.

questions.q: Which describes the author's literary right?
questions.e: "L stays, F pays." The financial right is the temporary, inheritable one.

questions.q: How many Shariah reasons are given for recognising the patent right?
questions.e: Patent drops the "general custom ('urf)" reason that copyright and trade name both carry. The slides show four, adding 'urf, but the exam follows the notes.

questions.q: Which reason is NOT given for the legitimacy of the patent right?
o: Plagiarism and false attribution are forbidden
questions.e: Per the notes, 'urf is the intruder — the sharpest trap in Lecture 3. (The slides do list 'urf for patents; the exam follows the notes.)

questions.q: Which patent certificate does NOT protect an invention?
questions.e: The importation certificate is an exclusive commercial enterprise right for whoever first brings a foreign invention in.

questions.q: A certificate issued for an improvement to an already-certified invention is:
questions.e: F.L.A.I.: Full, Limited, Additive, Importation.

questions.q: What does a patent holder give in exchange for the right to exclude others?
o: An enabling disclosure of how the invention works
A limited licence to the state
questions.e: "Exclusivity in exchange for disclosure."

questions.q: The three components of a trade name are:
questions.e: M.S.L. Distinctiveness / attraction / surveillance are the trademark's three functions, one level down.

questions.q: Which condition is attached specifically to the trade name's Shariah ruling?
o: That it be registered with the state
That it not be based on cheating or gharar
That it not be sold or transferred
questions.e: Trade name is the only one of the three carrying an explicit stated caveat.

questions.q: Which verse is the textual root for collaborative insurance?
o: "Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden interest"
"Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly"
"Zakat expenditures are only for the poor and the needy"
questions.e: One verse, one word: cooperate.

questions.q: In the Aqilah system, who pays the blood money for accidental homicide?
questions.e: The diyah is distributed among the paternal male relatives, who then pay the victim's family.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three modern collaborative insurance systems?
questions.e: R.S.R. Marine insurance is where commercial insurance began, in 15th-century northern Italy.

questions.q: Commercial insurance reached Islamic countries in which century, and under what name?
questions.e: It began as marine insurance in 15th-century northern Italy and transferred in the 19th century AD.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the five conditions of the risk?
o: The risk must not be intentional
The risk must be insurable at a fixed premium
The risk must be a future event
questions.e: U.N.P.F.R.: Uncertain, Not intentional, not Prohibited by law, Future, Regular/ordinary.

questions.q: A company insures its car against liability for damage the vehicle causes others. This is:
questions.e: P.P.L. — People and Property protect you; Liability protects others from you.

questions.q: If a commercial insurer pays the beneficiary back exactly what was paid in, which riba is involved?
questions.e: More than paid = fadl; exactly what was paid = nasī'ah; nothing paid = the company took the money illegitimately.

questions.q: An employer gives staff health insurance free as a company benefit. Under which exception is this permitted?
questions.e: D.N.F. "Free" removes the premium-for-payout exchange entirely.

questions.q: Which characteristic of transactions explains why analogy can extend a ruling to a case no text ever named?
o: They rest on general bases and principles
They are based on reasons and benefits
They are both flexible and constant
questions.e: Because the rulings are caused and benefit-bearing, the cause can be found in a new case.

questions.q: Incorporeal rights sit at the bottom of the rights hierarchy. Trace their full path from the top.
questions.e: Civil, then private, then financial, then the third of the three financial rights.

questions.q: A single modern contract that merges selling and renting is both a Lecture 1 category and a Lecture 3 topic. Which case of the definition does it illustrate?
o: Transactions formulated from several old forms combined
questions.e: Leasing contracts merging sale and rent are the textbook example of case 4, alongside murabaha.

questions.q: Retirement insurance is said to contain no gharar. Why?
o: Because the state guarantees the payout
Because it is a donation contract, and labour are both insured and insurer
Because the pension amount is fixed in advance
questions.e: A donation contract removes the compensation-for-price exchange that gharar attaches to.

questions.q: Which of these is prohibited even though the name suggests otherwise — per the hadith about drinking khamr under another name?
questions.e: Changing the name never changes the ruling; interest remains riba.

questions.q: Both copyright and trade name include a Shariah reason that patent omits. Which is it?
questions.e: Patent is recognised for three reasons only; 'urf is the one it drops. (The slides list 'urf for patents too; the exam follows the notes.)

questions.q: The Ash'arites pooling their food is cited as an example of:
questions.e: The Prophet ﷺ praised them: "they are of me, and I am of them."

questions.q: What happens to a collaborative insurance fund's surplus after all claims are settled?
o: The managing company keeps it as its administration fee
It belongs entirely to the participants, who may take it back or roll it forward
It is split evenly between the company and participants
questions.e: The company may administer the surplus and its investment interest, but keeps none of it. The slides add that the managing body may deduct a sum for its management effort only.

questions.q: Which principle allows a jurisprudent to treat a newly invented financial instrument as permissible in the absence of any text about it?
o: Al-ibāḥah — permissibility is the original rule
questions.e: No evidence of prohibition means permissible — for transactions, not for worship.

questions.q: Mandatory car insurance in a country where only commercial cover is available falls under which exception?
questions.e: Necessity is a classic fiqh override; the lecture names exactly this scenario.

questions.q: Which is the lecture's definition of a security?
o: A financial instrument representing an ownership position or a credit, issued by companies or governments as shares or bonds and traded on the bourse
Any physical commodity traded through a futures contract
A government guarantee attached to a company's debts
A loan contract between a bank and a single borrower
questions.e: Four working parts: a financial instrument, representing ownership or a credit, issued by companies or governments, traded on the bourse.

questions.q: A shareholder and a bondholder stand in which positions towards the issuer?
o: The shareholder is a part-owner; the bondholder is a creditor
The shareholder is a creditor; the bondholder is a part-owner
questions.e: “Title = Take part, Debt = Deliver back.” A title deed is ownership; a debt deed is a loan the issuer must repay.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three facts the slide gives about shares (E.V.D.)?
o: A specific amount paid on a certain date plus interest
Equal parts of the company's capital
questions.e: A fixed amount on a set date plus interest describes a bond. Shares are Equal parts, Voting, Dividends.

questions.q: Why is a bond usually issued?
o: To give the public voting rights
To distribute surplus profits to owners
To divide the capital into equal parts
Because the company needs a loan to expand its business
questions.e: A bond is the company borrowing; dividing capital into equal parts is what shares do.

questions.q: In a regular market, why do prices of the same goods tend to become uniform?
o: Buyers and sellers deal with each other freely, so nobody can charge much more than the next seller
Brokers set a single price each morning
Goods are kept in one central warehouse
questions.e: “Free contact → one price.”

questions.q: Where does the word “bourse” come from?
o: An inn in Bruges, Belgium — Huis Ter Beurze, founded in 1285 by Robert van der Buerze
The London Stock Exchange in the 18th century
A Latin word for a trading floor
questions.e: Inn → Purse → Bourse. Bruges gives the name; Paris (18th century) drives modern European growth. Don't swap the cities.

questions.q: What is the difference between a broker and a dealer?
o: There is no difference — the words are synonyms
A broker trades for their own account; a dealer trades for clients
A broker trades for a client; a dealer trades for their own account
Brokers trade only bonds; dealers trade only shares
questions.e: Broker = on Behalf of someone else. Dealer = Does it for themselves.

questions.q: How are commodities such as gold or oil traded on an exchange?
o: Only by physical delivery on the trading floor
They are never traded on an exchange
questions.e: S.B.C.F. — the catch is that commodities trade via futures, and forex usually lives in its own market.

questions.q: Which difference between a regular market and a bourse do exam questions lean on most?
o: Deals in the bourse can be speculation on price differences without paying the price or delivering the goods
The bourse only sells goods in front of the dealers
The bourse is always closed on weekends
questions.e: The slide says “can be”, not “always” — real purchases still happen on an exchange too.

questions.q: In a stock market, where are the goods being traded usually kept?
o: Right in front of the dealers
With the buyer before the deal
questions.e: M.L.I.R. — Location: in a regular market the goods are present; in a bourse they are stored elsewhere.

questions.q: What is a share, in one idea?
o: A deed of ownership in a company's capital, so the owner shares in profit and loss
A government guarantee of the company's debts
A promise to deliver goods at a future date
A loan the company must repay with interest
questions.e: Hold that one idea and every ruling in the lecture follows from it.

questions.q: “Indivisible against the company” means:
o: A share can never be sold
If several people share one share, only one of them represents them before the company
The company can never issue new shares
questions.e: E.I.T.N. — Equal, Indivisible, Tradable, Nominal value. Bonds carry the same four traits.

questions.q: Which value of a share is printed on the deed and does not change?
questions.e: N.I.R.M.: Nominal is printed, Issue is offered, Real is worth, Market is traded.

questions.q: A share's real value is calculated from:
o: The legal minimum set by law
Supply and demand on the exchange
questions.e: Real value comes from the balance sheet; market value comes from the exchange. Both move, for different reasons.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a right of an ordinary shareholder?
o: A fixed profit whether the company makes a profit or a loss
Suing board members for liability over their errors
Voting in the general assembly, one vote per share
Priority in subscription when new shares are issued
questions.e: A fixed profit regardless of the result is a feature of preferred shares — and it is exactly why they are forbidden.

questions.q: What is the first reason the lecture gives for forbidding preferred shares?
o: A fixed profit regardless of profit or loss is riba
They are issued only to foreigners
questions.e: Riba is the first reason; treating shareholders unequally, against the justice Islam requires, is the second.

questions.q: Why are enjoyment shares not permissible?
o: Because they can only be held by the government
Because they are issued for non-cash assets
Once the holder recovers the share's value they are no longer a partner, so further profit is illegitimate — and the lottery adds gharar
Because they carry no voting rights at all
questions.e: Consuming others' wealth unjustly, plus the uncertainty of choosing who is repaid by lottery.

questions.q: A company's core business is halal, but it takes interest-bearing loans in some of its transactions. Is dealing in its shares permissible under the lecture's conditions?
o: Yes, as long as the shares are ordinary
Only if the shares are bought in installments
Yes, because the core business is halal
No — the company must not deal in riba, even in some of its transactions
questions.e: “Halal, Clean, Clear, Not-P, Not-E.” Halal activity alone is not enough; the company must also be clean of riba.

questions.q: Which of these is permissible when trading shares?
o: Paying for a share in installments over time
Selling a share you do not yet own
Buying shares with an interest-bearing loan
questions.e: Installments are allowed. What is forbidden is borrowing with interest to buy, and selling what you don't own.

questions.q: A long-term investor holds shares in a Saudi company for its dividends. How is zakat paid?
o: The investor pays on market value every month
No zakat is due directly from the shareholder, provided the company pays zakat on its shareholders' behalf
Zakat is never due on shares
The investor pays on nominal value once a lunar year
questions.e: Hold → the company pays. Trade → you pay on market value once a lunar year.

questions.q: Which is the lecture's definition of bonds?
o: Transferable deeds issued by companies or governments representing long-term loans for incremental financial revenue, usually sold by public subscription
Certificates of ownership in a cooperative fund
Deeds representing equal units of ownership in a company's capital
questions.e: Same four traits as shares (E.N.T.I.) — but the substance is the opposite: debt, not ownership.

questions.q: Investment certificates “with increasing value and lottery draws” are:
o: A permissible product because the prize replaces interest
Still interest on a loan, with a lottery added on top
A government gift with no return
questions.e: Every one of the three types still pays interest on a loan; type c simply adds prize draws.

questions.q: Which describes treasury bills?
o: Issued by companies for ten years with high revenue
Issued by the government, usually for three months, sold by tenders, with very high liquidity but scant revenue
Issued by banks to shareholders as dividends
questions.e: T-bills = Three months, Tenders, Top liquidity — the best-seller for commercial banks despite the low yield.

questions.q: A holder pays 900 SAR for a 1,000 SAR bond redeemable with an issue premium. On what is interest calculated?
o: No interest is paid on this type
questions.e: The holder gains twice: interest on money never paid, plus the 100 SAR premium returned at maturity.

questions.q: A guaranteed bond with a “real” guarantee is backed by:
o: A mortgage on the company's real estate
questions.e: Personal guarantee = government or bank; real guarantee = a mortgage.

questions.q: When a company is dissolved, who is repaid first?
questions.e: “Debt, Fixed, Silent, First.” Shareholders get nothing until bonds and debts are paid.

questions.q: What rights does a bondholder have in the company's general assembly?
o: None — no assembly, no vote, no control
questions.e: The bondholder is Silent in the company.

questions.q: According to the hadith of Jabir in Sahih Muslim, who is cursed in a riba transaction?
o: Only the one who takes it
The one who takes it and the one who pays it only
The one who takes it, the one who pays it, the one who records it and the two witnesses
questions.e: “They are all the same.” Four are named, not just the lender.

questions.q: What is the legitimate alternative for a company in deficit?
o: Raise equity — issue new shares, or form joint ventures and partnerships
Advance the zakat of its shareholders
Issue more bonds at a lower rate
questions.e: For companies, one answer: shares, not bonds.

questions.q: The Prophet ﷺ taking the zakat of his uncle Al-Abbas two years in advance supports which government alternative?
questions.e: “Loan, Zakat, Give, Tax” — a good Loan, early Zakat, public Giving, exceptional Tax.

questions.q: In leasing (ijarah), what is actually transferred to the lessee?
o: A known benefit or usability of the asset for a specified period
The right to sell the asset
questions.e: The benefit is sold, not the asset, for a specified period and an agreed rent.

questions.q: Which party is the lessor?
questions.e: Lessor = the Owner (both have an “o”); lessee = the user, the tenant.

questions.q: The hadith qudsi used as evidence for leasing condemns:
o: One who returns a leased asset late
One who leases a house above market rent
One who hires a workman, takes full work from him and does not pay his wages
One who repairs a rented asset without permission
questions.e: Sahih al-Bukhari. Hiring is a recognised contract, and withholding the agreed payment is a grave sin.

questions.q: Who bears ownership risk and structural repairs in a lease?
questions.e: The tenant only does ordinary maintenance. Pushing major repairs onto the tenant is one reason the ownership-lease fails.

questions.q: In a lease ending with ownership as banks usually offer it, the “rent” is typically:
o: Zero until the end of the term
questions.e: The payments really include the buyer's equity — that is the first problem (Overpay).

questions.q: What is the key difference between an installment sale and a lease ending with ownership?
o: Only the installment sale aims at ownership
Installment sale: one contract, owned on day one. Ownership-lease: two contracts, owned on the last day
Only the ownership-lease is paid over time
questions.e: Same goal, same payments, different timing of ownership.

questions.q: How many contracts does a standard lease involve, compared with a lease ending with ownership?
questions.e: The ownership-lease adds a final transfer contract; the standard lease is a tenancy for the whole term.

questions.q: What is the core problem with the commonly practised lease ending with ownership?
o: The bank owns the asset during the term
It is only offered for cars
A contradiction between its name and its reality — it is called a lease but is really a sale
questions.e: “Overpay, Unclear, Unfair” — all three come from calling a sale a lease.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four conditions that make a leasing-based sale permissible?
o: A down payment is taken at the start to secure the bank
Ownership passes at the end by gift or a nominal-price sale
Each installment is fixed, with no increase for delay
questions.e: The fourth condition is the opposite: NO down payment, so the tenant loses nothing if they can't finish.

questions.q: Under the permissible form, how does ownership pass to the tenant at the end?
o: Automatically with the last rent payment, inside the lease
As a gift, or by sale at a nominal price, according to the earlier promise
Only if the tenant pays the full market price again
questions.e: “Period, Price, Pass, No down payment.”

questions.q: What is the evidence from the Quran that sale is permissible?
o: “Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden interest” (al-Baqarah 2:275)
“Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly”
questions.e: The second piece of evidence is the hadith on the option to cancel before the parties separate.

questions.q: According to the hadith in Bukhari and Muslim, until when may both parties annul a sale?
o: For three days after the contract
As long as they have not separated, or if it is a sale with an option to cancel
Never — a sale is binding on offer
questions.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 2112 / Sahih Muslim 1531.

questions.q: Which of the seven conditions of sale does the whole Murabaha section turn on?
o: Ownership — the seller owns the goods at the time of the contract
questions.e: A bank that sells before it owns breaks condition 4 — that is why the bank must buy first.

questions.q: “The goods and the price are clearly specified — type, quantity, weight or description” is which condition?
questions.e: “Can Legal Owners Deliver Known Items Now?” — Known is knowledge, to prevent dispute.

questions.q: An item sells for 50,000 riyals cash or 60,000 riyals over a year. What is the ruling?
o: Permissible, on condition that the price is fixed and cannot grow if payment is late
Permissible only if paid in gold
Riba — any increase for time is forbidden
questions.e: The extra is part of a sale price fixed at the contract. It becomes riba only if the debt grows because of late payment.

questions.q: How many parties does Murabaha involve as Islamic banks practise it today?
o: Three — customer, bank and original seller
Four — customer, bank, seller and guarantor
questions.e: Originally it was a simple two-party cost-plus trade.

questions.q: Before the bank's first contract, the customer's promise to buy is:
o: Legally binding, and the bank takes a deposit
Not legally binding, and the bank may not take any money from the customer
questions.e: “Don't sell what you don't have.” Breaking the promise could still be sinful if it harms a party.

questions.q: Once the bank has bought the commodity, what happens to the customer's promise?
o: The bank must refund the customer
It becomes binding — the customer buys or pays compensation
questions.e: Promise, Purchase, Profit — one promise and two contracts, always in that order.

questions.q: Which is a condition of Murabaha's second contract?
o: The goods are not items that must be exchanged hand-to-hand, like gold or dates
The bank may not take any guarantee
The profit is listed as interest separate from the base price
The price increases if payments are late
questions.e: “Agree, Bundle, Freeze, Avoid, Secure.” The bank may take a guarantee or mortgage.

questions.q: What distinguishes Murabaha from a direct installment sale?
o: Murabaha has three parties, a promise plus two sales, and the cost and markup are disclosed
Only the installment sale allows deferred payment
Murabaha allows the price to rise on late payment
questions.e: Shared rule: the price is fixed at the contract in both.

questions.q: Sara loads 2,000 riyals onto a card and spends only from that balance. What is the ruling on using it?
o: Permissible, because it works like cash and involves no loan
Not permitted, because every card is a form of interest-based loan
Permissible only if she settles the balance within forty days
Disliked, because the card’s limit is not renewed automatically
questions.e: A covered card is functionally equivalent to paying in cash and involves no loan (qard).

questions.q: A card’s balance must be paid in full within 40 days, and the limit returns only once it is settled. Which card is this?
questions.e: Instant credit is paid in full by the due date; the limit is not restored until the balance is settled.

questions.q: A customer repays in monthly installments with interest, and the limit renews as payments continue. The ruling on this card?
o: Permitted, if the interest rate is low and is fixed
Permitted, because the limit renews with each payment
Not permitted, because of riba on deferred payments
Permitted, as long as the installments stay on time
questions.e: Revolving credit involves interest on deferred payments, so it is not permitted.

questions.q: An instant-credit card has no interest during the grace period but stipulates a fee for late payment. Does it meet the conditions?
o: Yes: the fee applies only if the holder pays late
Yes: an instant-credit card is always permissible
No: instant-credit cards are forbidden in every case
No: a stipulated late charge is a forbidden element
questions.e: Stipulating a penalty or extra charge for payment delays is one of the forbidden elements.

questions.q: In the five parties to a card transaction, which one is the acquirer?
questions.e: The issuer is the client’s bank; the acquirer is the merchant’s bank.

questions.q: Which order is correct for a card transaction, after the purchase and receipt?
o: Issuer pays the merchant directly, and the merchant’s bank then bills the cardholder
Merchant’s bank seeks clearance, issuer pays, merchant’s bank is paid, issuer collects
Issuer collects, merchant’s bank seeks clearance, global organization pays the issuer
Global organization collects from the cardholder, then pays the merchant directly
questions.e: Clearance goes through the global organization; the issuer pays it, it pays the merchant’s bank, and the issuer collects from the cardholder.

questions.q: Omar’s card contract stipulates interest, but he always pays within the grace period and never pays any. The Fiqh Council’s ruling?
o: Permissible if he pays at the first opportunity
Permissible for purchases, but not for withdrawals
Not permissible to issue or use it
Permissible, as he never pays interest
questions.e: The resolution forbids it even if the holder is determined to pay within the free grace period.

questions.q: A bank charges a fixed fee for issuing a card. When is that fee permissible?
o: When it rises with the cardholder’s credit limit
When the cardholder has agreed to it in writing
When it is collected only in the first year
When it is based on the real cost of the service
questions.e: Set issue and renewal fees are allowed on the basis of the real cost of the services.

questions.q: A store adds 3% to card purchases so that the bank’s commission is covered. Why is the bank’s commission now a problem?
o: The business must sell at the same price as for cash
The bank may never take commission from a business
The commission should be charged to the cardholder
The store ought to pay the global organization first
questions.e: The bank may take commission so long as the business sells at the same price as transactions for cash.

questions.q: A bank charges a cash-withdrawal fee of 2% of the amount withdrawn. Why does that conflict with the resolution?
o: Only the global organization may charge any such fee
Fees must not be tied to the amount of the loan
Cash can never be withdrawn using a credit card
Withdrawal fees must be paid by the merchant’s bank
questions.e: A withdrawal is a loan; set fees must have nothing to do with its amount or period, and anything above actual cost is riba.

questions.q: Why does the Council forbid buying gold with an uncovered card?
o: Because card fees apply to gold
Because gold cannot be priced in riyals
questions.e: Point 4 of the resolution gives the delayed payment as the reason.

questions.q: Lina is offered a job selling a revolving credit card. What is the ruling on taking it?
o: Permissible, because she will not use the card herself
Permissible, provided that her salary comes from lawful work
Permissible, provided that customers understand the interest
Not permissible, because it helps in sin and transgression
questions.e: Marketing a haram type of card helps in sin; the hadith of Jaabir curses all who enable riba.

questions.q: Per the lecture’s definitions, placing money on who will win tonight’s match is...
o: Betting: risking money on an event decided by others’ effort
Gambling only if it takes place inside of a licensed casino
A permitted contest because the result depends on real skill
A sale, because the money is exchanged for a promised result
questions.e: Betting risks money on a future event that depends on other people’s effort.

questions.q: Which of these is listed in the lecture as a non-casino gambling game?
questions.e: Lotteries, pull-tab games and scratch cards are listed among non-casino games.

questions.q: A shop raises its usual prices and enters each buyer in a prize draw. How does the lecture classify this?
o: A sponsored contest, since the shop gives prizes
Permissible, as long as the prize is not cash
A form of gambling, since buyers fund the prize
An excluded store reward, since goods are sold
questions.e: No one can enter without buying, and the raised price contributes to the prize.

questions.q: A TV show charges viewers per text message to enter its prize draw. This is...
o: Allowed if the charge is small
questions.e: Competitions requiring payment for a call, message or other financial cost are listed forms.

questions.q: In the verse on gambling, what are al-Ansaab and al-Azlaam?
o: Sacrifices for idols and arrows for seeking luck
Types of intoxicants and types of card games
Two kinds of prize allowed in the archery contest
Sacrifices at Hajj and arrows used for hunting
questions.e: The verse explains al-Ansaab as sacrifices for idols and al-Azlaam as arrows for seeking luck or decision.

questions.q: Friends play for no money, but the game regularly causes arguments and makes them miss prayer. The ruling?
o: Disliked, but it is never truly forbidden
Not allowed, even with no monetary wager
Allowed, because no money changes hands
Allowed, if they agree to stop arguing
questions.e: The verse’s reasons, not only the money, are behind the prohibition.

questions.q: Which is one of the stated wisdoms behind the ban on gambling?
o: It shrinks what banks can earn in interest
It reduces the money collected through zakat
Earnings come from luck rather than hard work
It raises the price of goods in the market
questions.e: Gambling makes a person rely on luck and wishful thinking instead of hard work.

questions.q: A company donates a prize for a free university quiz. Why is this outside gambling?
o: The contest is educational and takes place on a campus
The prize is given as goods rather than as a cash sum
All contests that take place at universities are exempt
A non-participant funds it, so no contestant risks loss
questions.e: With third-party sponsorship, competitors do not contribute to the prize pool.

questions.q: Competitors in a horse race each contribute to the prize. Why is this allowed when the same arrangement in chess is not?
o: The hadith excepts camel-racing, horse-racing and archery
Horse racing depends on luck much less than chess does
A horse race always has a third-party sponsor behind it
Chess is forbidden in itself, with or without any prize
questions.e: Contestant-funded prizes are a classical exception for horse racing, camel racing and archery only.

questions.q: According to Ibn al-Qayyim, why were those contests permitted?
o: To entertain the people during Eid
To support trade between the tribes
To raise funds for the needy and poor
questions.e: He says they were permitted to encourage Muslims to learn horse-riding and prepare for Jihad.

questions.q: A store gives a voucher to anyone spending over 500 riyals, at no extra charge. How is this classified?
o: Gambling: customers must spend money to receive it
Excluded: only because it is under 500 riyals in value
Excluded: the customer pays only for the goods
Gambling: the voucher’s value is unknown beforehand
questions.e: Promotional vouchers carry no extra charge for entry, so there is no element of unlawful risk.

questions.q: A free contest makes participants forfeit a deposit if they lose. Which condition does it fail?
questions.e: Each contestant must win a prize or leave without a loss.

questions.q: A distributor earns on her own sales and a percentage on the sales of those she recruited. This describes...
questions.e: MLM distributors earn from personal sales and from sales by their recruits.

questions.q: Which is named in the lecture as a company using MLM?
questions.e: Avon, Telecom Plus and Discovery Toys are the named examples.

questions.q: Why do MLM distributors keep hiring new workers?
o: New recruits take over the distributor’s existing debt
The law requires a minimum number in each sales network
More layers bring greater commissions for early joiners
The company’s rules require a new hire every single month
questions.e: As layers increase, early joiners earn greater commissions, which drives recruitment.

questions.q: A program promises returns mainly for signing up new members and has no real product. It is...
questions.e: Returns primarily for enrolling new people, not for selling real products, define a pyramid scheme.

questions.q: Why does a pyramid scheme inevitably fail?
o: Recruitment becomes mathematically impossible to sustain
Its products are too expensive to keep in regular stock
The commissions that it pays are taxed at the highest rate
Its top members retire and take the customer lists away
questions.e: As recruitment expands, the model quickly becomes mathematically impossible to sustain.

questions.q: Where does the money flow in a pyramid scheme?
questions.e: Pyramid schemes involve money flowing exclusively upward, with no genuine sale of products.

questions.q: Which row of the comparison chart is the same for MLM and pyramid schemes?
questions.e: They differ in law and in setup, but the ruling in Islam is the same for both.

questions.q: “This MLM is a legal, registered company selling real products, so it must be halal.” What is wrong with this?
o: MLM companies are always illegal under the law
Registered companies may not sell real products
Selling real products is what makes MLM forbidden
Legal status does not settle the ruling in Islam
questions.e: MLM is legal in law but forbidden in Islam, because the drive is commission rather than the product.

questions.q: What is the main reason given by the Standing Committee for the prohibition?
o: The drive is commission, not the product
The goods are priced above the market
The distributors are not paid a salary
The companies are based outside the region
questions.e: Because the focus is commission and not the product, it leads to the forbidden deeds listed.

questions.q: Which set lists the three forbidden elements?
o: Gharar, monopoly, and breach of contract
Usury, gharar, and taking money unjustly
questions.e: The slide lists usury, gharar and taking people’s money unjustly.

questions.q: A company requires new members to buy a starter kit before they can sell. Which condition does it fail?
questions.e: Joining must be entirely free, with no required fees or mandatory purchases.

questions.q: A free program sells real products but also pays you on your recruits’ sales. What must change for it to be permissible?
o: Charge a small fee for joining the program
Pay the recruits a little more than the seller
Limit the network to three levels of recruits
Pay commissions on direct, personal sales only
questions.e: Commissions are paid solely on direct, personal sales, with no multi-tier payouts.

questions.q: Traditionally, what did a trader have to buy to become a member of an exchange?
o: A bond issued by the exchange
A licence from the central bank
A share in every listed company
questions.e: Leasing seats is less common now because most trading is electronic, though some exchanges still lease memberships or access rights.

questions.q: Which pair of words must never be swapped in an answer about securities?
questions.e: Shareholders get dividends as owners; bondholders get a fixed amount plus interest as lenders.

questions.q: Enjoyment shares are typically found in which kind of company?
o: Petroleum drilling and other depleting businesses
questions.e: A depleting business may not have enough left at closure, so it refunds shares annually, chosen by lottery.

questions.q: In-kind shares are issued in exchange for:
o: Non-cash assets such as property, equipment or intellectual property
questions.e: Cash shares are the most common; in-kind shares are paid for with assets. Both are permissible.

questions.q: Which investment certificate keeps the money with the bank for up to ten years, accumulating an ascending increase on principal and interest?
questions.e: Type b (current yield) pays a specified annual interest instead.

questions.q: What is the ruling on bonds, and why?
o: Permissible if issued by the government
Prohibited, because they are based on riba
questions.e: Riba is forbidden by the Quran and the Sunnah; the evidence given is the hadith of Jabir in Sahih Muslim.

questions.q: A client defaults in the final year of a common ownership-lease and loses both the payments and the car. Which problem does this illustrate?
o: Unfair — keeping purchase-level payments as rent is exploitation
questions.e: They paid purchase-level amounts without receiving ownership.

questions.q: Which of these is a tenant's obligation in an ordinary lease?
o: Reclaim the asset at the end
Pay the agreed rent on schedule and maintain the asset properly
questions.e: Tenant: pay, maintain, return. Owner: deliver usable, bear risk and structural repairs, reclaim.

questions.q: What must be checked before the bank signs the second contract with the customer?
o: That the customer has a guarantor
That the customer has paid a deposit
That the bank fully owns the commodity through its purchase order
That the seller has agreed to a lower price
questions.e: The condition people forget in the first contract.

questions.q: “The contract takes effect immediately, without delay or suspension” is which condition of sale?
questions.e: N for Now closes the seven conditions.
